Featured Project / Data Preparation & Quality Assurance

GlobalMart Data Cleaning & Quality Audit

Transforming an inconsistent retail operations spreadsheet into an analysis-ready, fully traceable Excel workbook—while carefully separating safe transformations from records that need human review.

Project type: Portfolio practice dataset · Deliverable: audited Excel workbook · Techniques: normalization, deduplication, validation, exception logging

Download Cleaned Excel ↧See Cleaning Evidence ↓Review Audit Findings ↓
2,090Original rows audited
35Exact copies removed
2,055Retained, traceable records
1,862Records requiring review
01 / Business Context

Why data quality matters

Retail analysts rely on trustworthy order records to evaluate delivery performance, stock availability, sales and profitability. Here, the source workbook combined inconsistent labels, formatting errors, incomplete fields, duplicate records and conflicting dates. Unchecked, these issues could lead to misleading KPIs.

Objective: create a reproducible, auditable starting point for downstream reporting—not claim unreliable values have been repaired.

Dataset scope

  • One raw worksheet with 22 columns and 2,090 order records.
  • Core domains: customer, geography, products, shipping, finance, inventory.
  • Original Notes field empty for all 2,090 records.
  • Cleaned view includes 21 business fields plus source-row and quality-control columns.
  • Input file supplied for this project; external provenance and commercial authenticity were not independently verified.
02 / End-to-end workflow

Cleaning process, column by column

Every example below is drawn from the uploaded workbook. Some steps intentionally record exceptions rather than overwrite uncertain source values.

01

Profile the raw workbook

Inspected 22 original columns and 2,090 data rows for completeness, consistency, duplicate entries, field types, and business-rule conflicts. The Notes column was empty in every record, so it was excluded from the analysis-ready view while remaining in the preserved raw sheet.

02

Remove exact duplicates, not every repeated ID

Removed 35 complete record repeats, retaining 2,055 rows. Another 45 rows repeated an Order ID but contained differing values; these were retained for manual investigation rather than assuming one record was wrong.

03

Standardize categorical fields

Trimmed leading/trailing spaces and collapsed repeated spaces in customer, region, country, product, supplier, warehouse, shipping mode, and delivery status fields. Mapped case variants such as EXPRESS to Express and synonyms such as Late Delivery to Late. Original blank categorical values were left missing.

04

Parse dates and audit chronology

Converted Order Date and Ship Date from mixed slash/hyphen day-first text to YYYY-MM-DD strings. Flagged 913 records where shipment precedes order and 1,830 records where the stated Days to Ship disagrees with the calculated calendar-day difference. Dates were not fabricated or reordered.

05

Convert numeric values and validate ranges

Parsed quantity, costs, prices, sales, shipping days, stock level, and damaged goods as numeric values. Missing or invalid entries remained blank and were flagged. Checked non-positive quantities, negative prices/costs, and damaged goods exceeding stock.

06

Reconcile sales, costs and profit

Tested Total Sales ≈ Quantity × Unit Price, Total Cost ≈ Quantity × Unit Cost, and Profit ≈ Sales − Cost, allowing $0.06 for rounding. Flagged 20 sales-total and 29 cost-total mismatches. The source financial amounts remain unchanged.

07

Publish cleaned output with traceability

Created Cleaned Data, Exception Audit, and Read Me worksheets alongside the original raw sheet. Every retained record has a source Excel row reference, quality notes, and a flag count to support follow-up.

03 / Validation Results

What the audit revealed

Counts below represent records with each issue and can overlap; do not sum them as unique records. After exact deduplication, 1,862 of 2,055 records have at least one flag and 193 have none under these checks.

Quality checkRows affected
Ship date earlier than order913
Days-to-ship/date disagreement1,830
Missing stock level29
Missing supplier26
Missing unit price23
Missing country22
Sales total mismatch20
Cost total mismatch29
Missing customer16
Negative unit cost7

Key finding

913 orders appear to ship before being placed. The source also reports 1,830 day-count discrepancies. These are not reliable grounds for measuring actual shipping efficiency until the date and Days to Ship fields are reconciled with business owners.

Duplicate-handling decision

35 identical rows were safely removed. 45 additional rows share Order IDs with other retained rows, but their values differ; deleting those could destroy real information. Keep and validate them separately.

04 / Column dictionary & policies

What changed—and what did not

Text standardized: Customer Name, Region, Country, Product Name, Supplier, Shipping Mode, Delivery Status, Warehouse.

Date structure: Order Date and Ship Date converted from day-first text into consistent ISO-formatted date strings (YYYY-MM-DD). These are strings for portability; Excel-native date retyping is an optional reporting step.

Numeric typing: Quantity Ordered, Unit Cost, Unit Price, Total Sales, Total Cost, Profit, Days to Ship, Stock Level, Damaged Goods.

Retained unchanged: Order ID, Product Category and actual source amounts unless simple numeric text conversion applied. The source Notes remains in the raw tab only.

Quality policy

  • Missing values stay missing; no imaginary customers, suppliers, stock or prices.
  • Impossible chronology is flagged, never shifted to an arbitrary date.
  • Financial discrepancies are flagged, not force-balanced.
  • Repeated IDs are reviewed separately from exact duplicate rows.
  • Source Row enables reproducibility and an investigation trail.
  • Quality Flag Count is the number of checks triggered, not an accuracy score.
05 / Deliverables & Next Actions

Usable output, with honest limitations

Outcome: a structured 2,055-row analysis view, preserved source sheet, exception audit, and written cleaning rules. This improves consistency and reviewability; it does not certify that the records are factually correct.

Excel workbook tabs

Raw Dataset (Messy) — unchanged source for traceability.
Cleaned Data — normalized fields, source row, flags.
Exception Audit — review list by source record.
Read Me — definitions, policies and caveats.

Recommended business follow-up

Confirm whether Days to Ship measures calendar days, processing time or an SLA. Reconcile reversed dates and repeated order identifiers against the order management system. Verify missing operational fields at source before building sales or delivery dashboards.

PROJECT 02 / EXCEL → POWER BI

E-commerce Sales Analytics & Dashboard

A complete sales reporting workflow using Excel for cleaning and feature preparation, followed by Power BI for interactive exploration of revenue, product categories, discounting, time trends and payment behaviour. Includes reproducible data evidence and an audit of the supplied Power BI report file.

Microsoft ExcelPower BIData CleaningData ModelingSales Analytics
3,660Transactions
₹757,278.08Net sales, Jan–Nov 2024
₹175,292.39Total discounts
5Power BI report pages

01. Business context & objective

The project explores how online transactions translate into revenue after discounting, which categories contribute most, how purchasing varies over time, and which payment methods consumers use. Its goal is to make the dataset reliable enough for consistent KPI reporting and to organize these questions into accessible Power BI report pages.

Scope: 3,660 records dated 01 Jan 2024–21 Nov 2024. Currency is Indian rupees (₹) as indicated by the source column names. This is a transaction-based sample; results should not be generalized to a real company's entire business.

02. Files & before/after structure

Raw source: ecommerce_dataset.csv — eight logical fields, purchase dates as text and currency/discount names containing spaces and punctuation. Cleaned output: Ecommerce sales dataset.xlsx — 16 reporting fields including calculated date attributes, discount amount and discount category. Both have 3,660 rows.

03. Excel data-cleaning process — evidence & explanations

The stages below are derived from a direct comparison of the submitted raw and cleaned files. They document what changed in the output, rather than claiming to reconstruct an unavailable Excel edit history.

01. Import and split the raw CSV

The raw file contains eight logical columns, but each entire line is surrounded by quotes. A default CSV import may treat that complete line as one field. The source was examined and parsed into User_ID, Product_ID, Category, Price (Rs.), Discount (%), Final_Price(Rs.), Payment_Method and Purchase_Date.

02. Rename columns and assign data types

The cleaned Excel workbook uses Power BI-friendly field names: Price (Rs.) → Price_Rs; Discount (%) → Discount_Pct; Final_Price(Rs.) → Final_Price_Rs. Price and final price became numeric currency values, discounts became numbers, and purchase dates were converted from DD-MM-YYYY text to genuine dates. Other categorical fields were retained.

03. Build a date analysis layer

Year, Month_Num, Month_Name, Quarter, Week_Number and Day_of_Week were added based on Purchase_Date. Month_Num supports correct January–December ordering in Power BI rather than alphabetical sorting of month names.

04. Calculate discounts and reporting bands

Discount_Amount_Rs was added as Price_Rs − Final_Price_Rs; Discount_Band groups each transaction into No Discount, Low (1–10%), Medium (11–20%), High (21–30%) and Very High (31–50%). The uploaded dataset uses these five band categories.

04. Field-level transformation log

Source / fieldCleaned columnTransformation
Price (Rs.)Price_RsRenamed and validated as numeric
Discount (%)Discount_PctRenamed and validated as numeric percentage values
Final_Price(Rs.)Final_Price_RsRenamed and validated as numeric
Purchase_DatePurchase_DateParsed as DD-MM-YYYY dates
NewDiscount_Amount_RsDerived from listed price minus final price
NewYear, Month_Num, Month_Name, Quarter, Week_Number, Day_of_WeekCalculated from Purchase_Date
NewDiscount_BandCategory based on discount percent

Unchanged business identifiers and dimensions: User_ID, Product_ID, Category, Payment_Method. There are seven categories and five payment methods in the dataset.

05. Quality assurance & validation

Independent review confirmed 3,660 records in both files, no missing values in the eight original fields, and no exact duplicate rows in the raw data. Original category labels and payment methods match the cleaned file row for row. Numerical price, final-price and percentage values also agree. Converted purchase dates were checked against the original DD-MM-YYYY strings.

Calculated discount amounts reconcile to Price_Rs − Final_Price_Rs within one paisa, allowing for stored currency rounding. As a separate source-consistency check, the raw final prices agree with Price × (1 − Discount%/100) within one paisa.

Important nuance: this was primarily a formatting, typing and feature-engineering job—not a missing-value repair or duplicate-removal project. The files do not prove which Excel functions were clicked during the original work, so formulas and UI actions have not been invented.

06. Moving the cleaned Excel file into Power BI

  1. Load the cleaned Excel table into Power BI Desktop.
  2. Verify numeric currency columns, date values and categorical fields in the model.
  3. Use the prepared date attributes for month, quarter and day-of-week analyses.
  4. Build revenue and order KPIs plus charts for categories, discount bands, purchasing trends and payment options.
  5. Use slicers to compare different segments, then arrange the report into a five-page navigable experience.

I inspected the internal metadata in the uploaded Power BI .pbix, which confirms these five pages and their visual types. A .pbix is an editable Power BI source file; its report cannot be faithfully rendered as screenshots in this website environment. See the five-page visual analysis below.

Report pageBusiness question / visuals
OverviewRevenue, discounts, average order value, order count and high-level category and monthly visuals
Category AnalysisCategory ranking, net revenue, category comparison and discount percentage
Discount AnalysisPerformance by discount band, order volume and average order value
Time TrendsQuarterly, monthly and day-of-week purchasing patterns
Payment BehaviourRevenue and average order value across payment methods

07. Sales findings based on verified Excel records

Net sales: ₹757,278.08 from 3,660 transactions; gross listed value: ₹932,570.47; recorded discount amount: ₹175,292.39; average order value: ₹206.91.

Highest net-revenue category: Clothing, contributing ₹115,314.84 (15.2% of the dataset total).

Highest recorded monthly net sales: October at ₹76,034.51. November is partial, ending on 21 November, so its total is not directly comparable with full months.

Largest payment segment by net sales: Credit Card at ₹156,018.02.

08. Power BI visual analysis — five report pages

Each image below is a data-derived recreation of the analysis, based on the uploaded cleaned Excel data and the actual page/visual inventory extracted from the Power BI file. These are not screenshots directly exported from Power BI Desktop; the file does not provide native rendered screenshots in this environment. All financial comparisons use recorded net sales, not profit.

01 / Overview

Recreated from cleaned Excel data and verified PBIX report structure — not a native Power BI screenshot.
Insight from the visuals

The report compares gross listed sales of ₹932,570.47 with net realized sales of ₹757,278.08. Discounts account for ₹175,292.39, or 18.8% of gross value. Across 3,660 transactions, the mean recorded net sale is ₹206.91.

Business implication

The sales gap is driven by recorded discounts. Management should track gross value, discount spend and net sales together instead of relying on gross sales alone.

02 / Category Analysis

Recreated from cleaned Excel data and verified PBIX report structure — not a native Power BI screenshot.
Insight from the visuals

Clothing contributes the largest net sales at ₹115,314.84, representing 15.2% of the total. Categories differ in both number of transactions and average ticket value, so a sales ranking alone does not identify the strongest unit economics.

Business implication

Prioritize category-level revenue and average transaction value together; investigate lower-performing categories before allocating additional promotions.

03 / Discount Analysis

Recreated from cleaned Excel data and verified PBIX report structure — not a native Power BI screenshot.
Insight from the visuals

The most revenue-generating discount band is Low (1-10%), contributing ₹224,290.49. Total discounts amount to ₹175,292.39. A higher discounted-band sales total does not demonstrate that discounting caused additional purchases.

Business implication

Test whether larger discounts meaningfully increase transaction volumes or revenue before expanding offers. Without cost or control-group data, profit uplift and promotion effectiveness cannot be established.

04 / Time Trends

Recreated from cleaned Excel data and verified PBIX report structure — not a native Power BI screenshot.
Insight from the visuals

Q3 has the highest recorded quarterly net revenue at ₹212,348.28. Oct shows the highest monthly revenue (₹76,034.51), while Sunday has the largest number of transactions (566).

Business implication

Use months and weekdays to plan monitoring and outreach, but normalize incomplete periods: the source ends in November 2024, so comparisons with full months require care.

05 / Payment Behaviour

Recreated from cleaned Excel data and verified PBIX report structure — not a native Power BI screenshot.
Insight from the visuals

Credit Card contributes the highest recorded net sales (₹156,018.02; 20.6% of the total). Cash on Delivery has the highest average recorded transaction value at ₹210.36. These figures reflect selected payment methods, not processing costs or payment failures.

Business implication

Maintain access to major payment options. Compare revenue share, ticket values and payment processing costs if operational data becomes available before recommending a payment channel shift.

Dashboard interpretation caution: Transaction records do not include cost of goods, traffic, conversion rate, product returns, payment failures, or controlled promotional experiments. The report can describe revenue patterns and associations, but cannot prove profitability or causality.

09. Overall business recommendations and limitations

  • Monitor net sales and discount cost together, instead of treating gross listed prices as realized revenue.
  • Use category and discount-band slicers to investigate where high discount rates coincide with weaker revenue outcomes.
  • Maintain stable month ordering using Month_Num; compare like-for-like date windows because November is incomplete.
  • Do not describe these results as profit or margin analysis: product costs are not provided.
  • Do not label recorded transactions as confirmed orders, conversions or customers beyond the available data definitions without validation.
